text:
### Observed differences

- Repetition of A25, A26 and A31 largely stopped in the later window: earlier each occurred about 3.4 times per trace and repeated within about 75 in 100 traces; later each occurred about 1.0 times per trace, with repeats in fewer than 1 in 100 traces. Every trace still contained all three activities in both windows. [OCC019, OCC020, OCC025]
- A31's outgoing transitions flipped: earlier about 71 in 100 led back to A25 and about 29 in 100 led to A20; later about 96 in 100 led to A20 and only about 4 in 100 to A25. [DIR020]
- A25 and A31 still co-occurred in every trace, but their relation changed from mostly interleaved or repeated (75 in 100 traces, fixed A25-before-A31 order in only 25 in 100) to a fixed A25-before-A31 order in 199 of 200 traces. [REL001]
- In the later window A31 followed A25 exactly two event positions later in about 92 in 100 traces (about 12 in 100 before), and the reverse follow, A31 then A25 within five steps, appeared in 150 traces before but in only one trace after (that after-figure rests on a single observation). [LAG001, LAG002]
- The event positions of A25 and A31 became about twice as tightly concentrated (spread, e.g. standard deviation, about 0.12 down to about 0.06), consistent with fewer repetitions rather than a relocation of the activities. [POS001, POS002]
- A32, A33, A35, A36, A37 and A38 occurred moderately less often in the later window (for example A33 in about 52 vs 44 in 100 traces; A35 about 1.75 vs 1.56 times per trace, with repeats in 43 vs 33 in 100 traces), while A10 and A11 repeated slightly more often (about 1.6 to 1.7 times per trace). [OCC009, OCC010, OCC026, OCC027, OCC028, OCC029, OCC030, OCC031]
- Several routing shares shifted moderately: A33 led more often to A34 than to A32 (about 53 to 58 in 100), A38 more often to A39 (about 55 to 67 in 100), A34 more often to A14 than to A15 (about 49 to 55 in 100), A22 more often to A19 (about 26 to 35 in 100), A19 less often to A23 (about 50 to 40 in 100), and A11 less often to A33 (about 32 to 26 in 100). [DIR009, DIR013, DIR014, DIR021, DIR022, DIR025]
- Participation moved a few points for some activities (up for A13 from 24 to 29, A14 from 49 to 55, A19 from 51 to 58 in 100 traces; down for A15 from 52 to 46 and A18 from 50 to 42 in 100), while the many remaining differences of roughly 1–4 percentage points across other activities and edges stayed at a level typical of sampling variation. [OCC012, OCC013, OCC014, OCC017, OCC018, OCC001, DIR012, DIR018]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the repetition of A25, A26 and A31 stopped in the later window: activities that earlier ran about three to four times per trace, with A31 usually leading back to A25 for another pass, now run exactly once per trace in the fixed order A25 then A31, with A31 continuing to A20 instead of returning to A25. The relational items show this directly — the reversal of A31's exit shares, the change from mostly interleaved/repeated to a single fixed order, the concentration of the A25→A31 distance at two positions, and the near-disappearance of the A31→A25 follow — and they agree with the occurrence drop at unchanged 100% participation; the exit shares even match the repetition rates (about 29 in 100 exits correspond to about 3.4 passes before, about 96 in 100 to about 1.04 after). Every item involved exceeds 199 of 200 random re-splits, and the after-window figures rest on 200 traces (208 observed outgoing transitions of A31), except the single-trace LAG002 after-figure, which DIR020 corroborates. Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish whether the repetition itself was removed or the choice at A31 changed so that it now almost always continues to A20; no relational item covers A26, whose involvement rests on its identical occurrence profile; and no chance-expectation baseline was provided, so the judgement rests on the size, directness and mutual consistency of the differences. [OCC019, OCC020, OCC025, DIR020, REL001, LAG001, LAG002, POS001, POS002]

The main competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is an upstream rerouting that sends every case through a single-pass variant of the same path; pure sampling fluctuation, by contrast, is implausible given that recurrence fell from 75 to under 1 in 100 traces and the A31→A25 follow from 150 traces to one. [OCC019, OCC025, LAG002]

Other differences: A32, A33, A35, A36, A37 and A38 occurred moderately less often in the later window, several routing shares shifted (A33 towards A34 over A32, A38 towards A39, A34 towards A14 over A15, A22 towards A19, A19 towards A16 over A23, A11 away from A33) with matching small participation shifts for A13, A14, A15, A18 and A19, and A10 and A11 repeated slightly more often. These may be downstream effects of the repetition change or separate adjustments, but the evidence does not connect them relationally to A25, A26 or A31, so they are not part of the main hypothesis. [OCC009, OCC010, OCC012, OCC013, OCC014, OCC017, OCC018, OCC026, OCC027, OCC028, OCC029, OCC030, OCC031, DIR009, DIR013, DIR014, DIR021, DIR022, DIR025]
